        <meta name="citation_description" content="Collection contains interview guide used to conduct semi-structured interviews with National Weather Service forecasters responsible for issuing tornado, flash flood, flood, and other hazards that can co-occur during hurricanes (29 interviews for Florence; 19 interviews for Harvey). Interviews were audio recorded, transcribed, and names removed. Questions focused on demographic and employment information, main concerns and impacts from hurricanes in the County Warning Area for each office; process of assessing and issuing warnings for different water and wind threats; policies and practices for communicating these threats, as well as mechanisms for dissemination (e.g. social media); and what worked/didn't work; and what information or tools forecasters wish they could have for the next hurricane.">

        <meta name="citation_title" content="Hurricane Harvey Twitter Data">
        <meta name="citation_publication_date" content="2021-11-04T19:18:59.409378">
        <meta name="citation_doi" content="10.17603/ds2-3rc2-qy38">
        <meta name="citation_description" content="Collected all tweets from a 12-day period from when Harvey first formed until remnants left the U.S. Tweets were collected using Twitter API searching for keywords of wind and water threats that co-occurred in the same tweet. Search terms included the following:  ((tornado OR #tornado OR \"funnel cloud\” OR funnelcloud) (\"flash flood\” OR flood OR flashflood OR \"storm surge\" OR stormsurge)). Tweets were classified into three categories: public user (e.g. seeking information and sharing personal experience), authoritative user (e.g. sharing information but not personal information), or other (e.g. private or deleted accounts and bots). After classification, Twitter was re queried via the API to collect contextual tweet streams (entire user history) for the 12-day period for public and authoritative users. As January 2021, the dataset contains 131,754 tweets from 233 authoritative users and 208,725 tweets from 337 public users.">

    <script type="module" id="js-open-pdfs-ext-links-new-window">
    import findLinksAndSetTargets from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/TACC/Core-CMS@v3.11.0-alpha.1/taccsite_cms/static/site_cms/js/modules/setTargetForExternalLinks.js';

    const pathsToRedirectsToExternal = [
        '/facilities/simcenter/',
        '/facilities/rapid-facility/',
        '/rw/simcenter-research-tools/',
        '/learning-center/simcenter-learning-tools/',
        '/community/mechs/',
        '/rw/user-guides/',
        '/help/user-guides/',
        '/help/getting-started/',
        '/rw/use-cases/',
        '/faq/',
    ];
    const pathsToPDFs = [
        /\.pdf/
    ];
    // NOTE: Some links have `target="_blank"` even though they should not
    const pathsOfManualNewTabLinks = document.querySelectorAll(
        '[target="_blank"]:not([aria-describedby])'
    );

    /** Adds accessibility attribute to links that open in new tab */
    function supportA11y( link ) {
        const hasA11yNote = link.querySelector('span.sr-only');
        const hasA11yDesc = link.hasAttribute('aria-describedby');

        if ( ! hasA11yNote && ! hasA11yDesc ) {
            link.setAttribute('aria-describedby', 'msg-open-new-window');
            if (window.DEBUG) {
                console.debug(`Link ${link} now has "aria-describedby"`);
            }
        }
    }

    /* To make certain links open in new window, and apply a11y attribute */
    findLinksAndSetTargets({
        pathsToForceSetTarget: [
            ...pathsToRedirectsToExternal,
            ...pathsToPDFs
        ],
        setTargetCallback: supportA11y,
    });

    /* To apply a11y attribute to manual new tab links */
    [ ...pathsOfManualNewTabLinks ].forEach( supportA11y );
</script><!-- https://medium.com/@svinkle/why-let-someone-know-when-a-link-opens-a-new-window-8699d20ed3b1#79b2 -->
